A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IA2 research work. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on classification and generation tasks with Qwen and Llama models, including performance comparisons, activation analyses and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3–6 and Appendices B–C, including accuracy, calibration and statistical significance results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same activation collection and alignment procedure followed by supervised fine-tuning. The objectives and the combined-loss variant discussed in Section 6 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same sentiment, news classification, true/false, multiple-choice, math and scientific QA coverage. The same out-of-distribution evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including ICL, SFT-only, IA2 variants and the soft-label knowledge-distillation baseline in Table 4. The comparisons using LoRA and (IA)3 are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–B retain the same sample selection, shot counts, model configurations, training settings, generation limits, answer parsing and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The activation-similarity and weight-subspace analyses, combined versus sequential training comparisons, LoRA ablations in Table 7 and ICL overfitting analysis in Figure 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-run averaging and standard deviations. Appendix B retains the same paired t-test procedure and significance reporting in Table 8.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries in Tables 1–20 and plotted results in Figures 1–6 are unchanged. No results, rankings or qualitative findings were added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the activation-similarity definition and the weight-subspace overlap formula are unchanged. Section 4 alters paragraph and equation spacing without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about distinct ICL/SFT functional behavior and improved accuracy and calibration from IA2 priming. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations involving activation alignment, weight subspaces and limited LoRA capacity are retained. Discussions of ICL overfitting, computational overhead, resource constraints and future improvements are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information in Section 5 and Appendices A–B is unchanged. The reproducibility statement retains the same code link and access information; changing 'code' to 'codes' adds no technical detail.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the cited-work set are unchanged. References move across page boundaries, but none are added or removed and the positioning relative to prior research is retained.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the preprint header with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', adds an acknowledgment to Andrea Wynn and makes small wording and punctuation edits on page 11. Section 4 separates the IA2 introduction into its own paragraph; the broader narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The header and arXiv stamp change, Section 4 adjusts paragraph and equation spacing, and the references reflow across pages 11–15. Figures, tables, captions and their placements are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the scientific content and supporting evidence, including all appendix analyses and results. The publication header, acknowledgment and limited formatting edits produce no meaningful net difference in the paper's overall quality.
